messages:
Marta Gomez: Quick question — I'm doing a 10-week split-residence project (Lisbon + SF) starting May 12. Do I need to change anything for the WFH allowance or payroll?
Oliver Chen: Congrats! For >30 days we usually trigger a payroll review. @Elena any other gotchas for a temporary dual residence?
Elena Kaur: Hey @Marta — nice, thanks for flagging. Short answer: yes, a few things. We treat this as a temporary dual-residence (we call it a 'split-residence buffer') and do two things: 1) prorate the monthly WFH allowance for any month you spend majority-time outside your declared primary homebase, and 2) run a tax-nexus screen with Finance for the country pair.
Raj Patel: +1. For Portugal<>US we need to check the 183-day rule and whether local payroll or remote contractor setup is required. If the screening raises a nexus, payroll will coordinate a cutover or ask for a short-term contractor engagement.
Elena Kaur: Action items for you @Marta: fill the Homebase Change form (link: https://ok.redwood/forms/homebase-change) with the dates and city addresses, and upload a copy of your travel plan. In the form, pick 'temporary split-residence' and put expected return date. That kicks off payroll + tax checks.
Marta Gomez: Cool — what's the stipend proration formula so I can plan?
Elena Kaur: Formula is simple: monthly_stipend * (days_in_primary_homebase / total_days_in_month). If you switch primary homebase mid-month we run proration pro-rata. Example we give in the form: `150 * (10/30) = 50` for days in-home.
PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: if you submit the Homebase Change form, the system will auto-create a ticket for Payroll (tag: payroll-review) and send you a checklist DM.
Raj Patel: Also ping payroll@redwood when you submit so we can prioritize the nexus screen. If we need local tax registration, timelines are usually 2–6 weeks.
Marta Gomez: Thanks — I'll submit the form today and cc payroll. Appreciate the example proration.
Elena Kaur: One more note: hardware shipping and benefits remain the same during the buffer; but if a payroll cutover happens we may adjust benefits tax treatment. We'll notify you before any change.
Marta Gomez: Got it. Will update here after submission.
